# social-service-ea per-operation parity backlog

Baseline: `decentraland/social-service-ea@b6b2cefefdf727b2ed47ddb887e77d226a41eea6`. The machine source is [parity.json](parity.json).

The source inventory contains **123 operations**: 5 api_auxiliary, 72 api_http, 6 json_stream, 6 rpc_stream, 27 rpc_unary, 5 uws_http, 2 websocket.

reviewed means the stated source/behaviour scope was compared; it never means exhaustive equivalence. known_gap names a remaining observed difference. not_reviewed requires an explicit comparison, even if a matching route or local test exists.

Source hashes include the pinned service registrations, handlers, stream definitions, lockfile and the installed framework code that supplies health, CORS, metrics and fallback handling. `tooling/social-service-parity.py --upstream <checkout>` re-derives that inventory; the default check validates its complete backlog, local evidence references and the 33-method protocol set and complete source-pinned social-service/error/color schema hashes without an external checkout. The only other schema import is the standard `google/protobuf/empty.proto`.

Executed upstream handler cases live in [source-cases.json](source-cases.json); their Protobuf bytes are replayed by `rpc_wire_answers_match_executed_upstream_source_cases`. Those cases use injected dependencies and do not prove deployed HTTP, Redis, SNS, PostgreSQL or live-client equivalence.

## Shared gaps and replacement requirements

These requirements remain open even when an operation's focused review passes. A local implementation or a matching fixture does not establish a completed cutover.

| Requirement | Status | Evidence and remaining work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `external-notification-consumers` | unverified | Configured friendship and all twelve community SNS producers preserve source raw fields, keys and recipient policies through the existing official SDK publisher. Source/local stub tests cover 100-recipient pages/messages, ten-message requests, failure isolation, opt-out independence and HTTP background versus voice-awaited execution. Existing deployed topic subscriptions, downstream consumers, retry timing and migration/cutover delivery remain unverified. Candidate SNS scheduling permits at most eight in-flight ten-entry requests per publish_batch invocation; source dispatches chunks without that concurrency bound. Result order, complete awaiting and failed-chunk isolation have real SDK/HTTP regressions. |
| `cross-replica-social-events` | unverified | Mutation fanout uses the existing core NATS link. Awaited publisher enqueue, synchronous targeted delivery and a 1,000-entry community work queue with at most min(4,pool size) SQL tasks deliver actual 1,000-update targeted/community bursts locally. Control traffic remains live; large public snapshots, process-local context restart and cache expiry are covered. Delivery remains transient and at most once. Deployed replica/consumer behavior, traffic beyond these measured bounds and outage/reconnect equivalence remain unverified. |
| `community-started-audience-lifetime` | unverified | Audience scope/generation/24-hour refreshed expiry persist in shared SQL. Restart, expiry, generation-CAS and retained immutable event snapshots pass local tests. Existing room state, external media continuity and deployed cutover remain unverified. |
| `referral-lifecycle` | unverified | Attribution/IP rejection, signup, UTC login days, guarded grants, artwork, email, handler-specific SQL errors and configured Slack effects have source-paired/local regressions. Slack keeps source payloads and empty-token serialization but deliberately bounds each effect to ten seconds, three attempts and a two-second Retry-After cap. Referral identity uses the TCP peer or explicitly trusted backend proxy X-Real-IP, and canonical historical inet aliases share a quota; these are intentional source differences. Sixteen executed numeric configurations cover source parser values, bigint rejection/overflow and login-day comparisons. Live providers, concurrent rate-limit ordering and stateful deployed cutover remain unverified. Referrer/IP quotas and milestone counts are serialized in SQL; tier-image and tier-notification work retain independent fail-fast completion. Actual source partial-failure receipts and local concurrent PostgreSQL cases are compared; simultaneous decision ordering is strengthened beyond source. A reward-tier grant retains reward_tier until its downstream notification and image complete. A committed pre-POST claim prevents concurrent or restarted workers from reissuing the non-idempotent provider request; a confirmed response is persisted before downstream work. With social writes enabled, a fleet-leased drain selects at most 64 due rewards per pass every 60 seconds, and failed attempts defer eligibility by one minute. The reward_paid receipt retains the tier, provider result and confirmed notification marker; an image retry skips a notification already recorded as delivered. Missing campaign configuration remains retryable before claiming. A claimed request without a confirmed response, including migrated historical pending rewards without a paid receipt, requires provider reconciliation and is not automatically retried; confirmed responses resume downstream delivery without another login. Notification publication can still be repeated after an ambiguous downstream failure, so exactly-once external delivery is not claimed. This recovery differs from the source, which commits the grant and does not retry a failed reward. Referral deny checks read the shared in-process explorer snapshot instead of fetching the list on each write. Every serving process refreshes the merged database mirror/local overlay every 30 seconds with a five-second pass timeout, even when mirrors or fleet jobs are disabled; failed refreshes retain the last snapshot. Reloads are serialized within each process. This is eventual propagation, not immediate revocation or identical source freshness. The receipt migration imports existing paid tiers and responses while preserving their notification completion marker. |
| `community-ranking-and-configured-moderation` | unverified | Dynamic moderators, ranking producers and configured AI compliance have source/local regressions. Provider probes cover active-bootstrap missing/empty strings, bodies above4MiB, headers-only600s timer, native10s connect/300s inactivity and AI metric outcomes. Delayed DNS, composed network phases and deployed credentials remain unverified. Existing lifetime ranking counters and watermarks have not been imported, so historical ranking equality is unverified. Local event collection bounds source keys and recurrence windows under one pass budget; pending-photo repair cycles bounded recent/cold cohorts and isolates slow/error rows. SQL and100k synthetic backlog measurements do not establish deployed freshness. Retry scheduling is an explicit target policy; physical filesystem stalls are not executed. |
| `shared-fixed-window-friendship-limit` | unverified | The implemented SQL limiter matches eight executed source/Redis scenarios plus concurrent replica, fixed-expiry and configuration regressions. Existing Redis counter state has not been imported or drained during a nonempty cutover; a fresh SQL counter resets the active window. |
| `cutover-with-existing-state` | unverified | No nonempty migration snapshot, deployed provider/edge configuration, active LiveKit call continuity, running-client comparison or rollback rehearsal has been supplied or executed. These are replacement acceptance requirements, separate from local contract tests. |
| `referral-external-cutover` | unverified | Configured official SQS/SNS transports preserve legacy raw events and attributes locally; ranking dispatch, friendship and community publication are wired. Deployed queue policies, topic subscriptions and credential access have not been exercised. Populated candidate additive upgrades pass synthetic tests; existing upstream progress/login-days/reward/email import and live cutover remain outstanding. Existing pending rewards without a paid receipt are quarantined by the additive receipt migration because their provider outcome cannot be inferred; reconcile them with the provider before clearing a claim or supplying a confirmed response. Live reconciliation and downstream duplicate-notification handling remain deployment gates. |
| `api-body-size-boundary` | known_gap | Configured HTTP_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES uses source prefix parsing and integer 1..16MiB admission. Declared oversize rejects before routing/auth; deferred reads preserve schema400 versus raw/multipart500 and independent multipart1MiB/thumbnail1..500KiB limits. Eighteen boot and 44 HTTP body cases replay through real drain/Normalize. Gateway-only authentication precedes mirror SQL and federation classification; client JSON uses its configured cap. Twelve additional actual-source server cases independently regenerate exactly, with eight healthy candidate exchanges and separate denied-role auth/SQL controls. Native aliases retain 1MiB fallback and buffer512KiB-before-auth federation contracts; confirmed gateway envelopes retain typed verification and512KiB cap after classification. Known differences remain: signed body-ignoring joins answer immediately in source but classification needs complete JSON, oversized incomplete envelopes can reject later, and unread fast chunked overflow uses different connection-close timing. Raw framing, longer transport lifetime and concurrent resource use remain unverified. |
| `shared-social-profile-cache` | unverified | RPC and community adapters share source 600-second SQL cache facts over the existing pool. Twenty-nine historical lookup steps, eight strict owner handler cases and eight mixed-case adapter steps pass source/local replay. Requested keys and Set deduplication preserve exact case; physical content-pointer lookup remains normalized. The mixed-case registry response is injected, so deployed registry case/order behavior is unverified. Existing Redis values and remaining TTL have not been imported or drained for cutover. |
| `community-dependency-error-boundaries` | unverified | All 37 community handlers preserve source message-only 500 for unexpected core SQL errors. Independently recaptured actual Node handlers receive a real node-pg exception through injected domain dependencies; candidate requests exercise restricted-role PostgreSQL faults and paired standing failures. Author community suite passes 184 cases, including unchanged federation error envelopes. Registry-read/provider/voice failure phases remain separate requirements; arbitrary driver error wording and deployed outages are not proven equivalent. Community AI compliance runs within a 60-second whole-effect bound (the source SDK allows three 600-second attempts); signed federation create/update envelopes take the same content check as the REST routes. Social answers also carry X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, which the source does not send. Community post creation answers a wallet with an active ban as the source answers one without a role (401), also when a member row was left beside the ban. |
| `rpc-ordinary-transport-backpressure` | known_gap | The existing Social opt-in writer bounds ordinary pending frames with the source adaptive count, retry/backoff/drain policy and accepted-once semantics. Fifteen supported-policy source traces replay; two additional cases document candidate startup rejection for maxBackpressure0 and computed nonfinite queue capacity where the source can admit unbounded buffering. WS_MAX_BACKPRESSURE uses a strict unsigned parser rather than native numeric-prefix/fraction/wrap conversion. Application writer admission/flush is measured separately from native uWS kernel behavior; deployed performance equivalence is unverified. Twenty executed source backpressure-number cases separate raw f64 queue capacity from native unsigned32 truncation/wrap. Prefix, fraction and representable wrap inputs are implemented; native-zero and nonfinite-capacity configurations remain unsupported and unaccepted, and kernel/performance equivalence remains unverified. A guarded frame holding the writer's admission turn is contention, not backpressure: ordinary frames behind it wait without spending retry attempts. The shared RPC server loop never awaits socket send admission; ServerReady, port, module and stream-open replies are spawned like unary responses. |
| `community-voice-status-failure-degradation` | unverified | Core community SQL and voice reads use separate queries on the same pool/config through existing VoiceDb methods. Companion voice SQL failures yield idle/empty, while core failures retain500; active filters return empty before core reads if their voice result is empty or failed. Twenty-nine actual-source component/handler/adapter cases cover companion SQL stages, core errors and direct-provider500; candidate regression pairs18 requests plus three dual-fault controls. Source errors are injected; target faults are real PostgreSQL permissions. Package community193/all-targets/module checks pass. Direct-provider transport, concurrent snapshots and deployed cutover remain unverified. Ordinary voice reads are bounded by returned page IDs; all-active scans remain global. |
| `social-client-artifact-cutover` | unverified | Signed Social paths match 81 source verifier decisions and real socket replays. The Bevy client preserves its connection URL while signing /; a native cryptographic unit covers standalone, mounted and query URLs. Deployed web artifacts must contain that update before strict server cutover. Cached/running clients, full Explorer, wasm and rendered /play behavior have not been exercised. Exact legacy mounted signing aliases are accepted alongside canonical source paths. Signed socket regressions cover old/new spellings and reject arbitrary proxy/header aliases; deployed cached artifacts and admitted client versions still need runtime comparison. |
| `social-initial-subscription-readiness` | known_gap | The Social subscription is registered and retained before its first readiness latch observes the existing broker fence. Both valid upgrades are refused before auth/slots until that latch; later outages retain transient at-most-once policy. Six actual source lifecycle stages and two candidate tests cover order and local-mode admission. Candidate startup responds empty HTTP 503 while the standalone source listener is not yet open; this operational difference is explicit and has no user acceptance verdict. |
| `community-fanout-whole-membership-failure` | unverified | Pinned logic/updates.ts gathers every membership page before delivery. Candidate snapshots eligible subscribers, completes all bounded 256-address probes before emitting, aborts all member-scoped delivery on any failed page and clears all isMember annotations on a failed public STARTED; public ENDED skips membership reads. Six independently recaptured actual-source cases and the owned-SQL second-page failure regression pass, including 513 eligible recipients and zero partial emissions. All seven fanout tests pass, including actual NATS. Fresh independent static review confirms the whole-audience fix; deployed failure behavior and final aggregate review remain unverified. |
| `configured-social-analytics-effects` | unverified | All 16 source analytics event kinds are connected at the 17 voice/community producer sites through the shared concrete adapter. Source captures cover 35 voice scenarios and 19 community scenarios; candidate regressions pair all 35 voice and 17 normal/no-op community scenarios, with nine separately paired PostgreSQL trigger cases for partial-write boundaries. Source SDK configuration, response cancellation, cross-host redirects and whole-chain deadlines are independently recaptured. Analytics retains its own provider profile; actual native-source probes pair10s connect,300s per-hop headers and the configured SDK deadline across redirects. Operator-configured provider destinations and x-token forwarding follow source behavior. Delayed DNS and combined clock phases remain unverified. The generic unconfigured monolith intentionally remains usable; each configured provider validates its own source required strings before serving (analytics its context, URL, token and ENV; AI compliance its OpenAI key; referral Slack ENV); ENV alone configures no provider, including at the actual Analytics::new constructor; an empty posture-injected analytics URL stays inactive. The candidate constructor regression shared_environment_alone_does_not_activate_analytics_but_partial_settings_fail covers empty/prd/dev ENV and rejects incomplete analytics-specific settings. Without OPEN_AI_API_KEY the node runs without the compliance provider and skips classification, where the source refuses to start. Deployed routing/provider behavior and transient-event cutover remain unverified. The six entry-wrapper cases preserve raw RPC recipient and HTTP private-call identifier spellings independently from normalized SQL/authorization/recipient keys. |
| `private-call-pending-expiry-start-order` | unverified | Pending calls keep both parties busy until the expiry sweep deletes them; starting a call never reclaims expired pending rows or emits their EXPIRED event. All 35 voice analytics/source scenarios are paired, including the expired-start case. Voice package 56 tests and comms voice-database seven tests pass. Production sweep timing and existing-state cutover remain unverified. |
| `private-call-disconnect-accepted-media` | unverified | Social disconnect finishes only pending calls. An accepted row, its two participants and media room remain until explicit media end; the owned-PostgreSQL regression and source domain captures match. Package voice 56 tests pass. Live clients and media-room cutover remain unverified. |
| `community-registry-read-failure-propagation` | unverified | The six V1 profile-enriched reads propagate existing registry batch read errors while cache writes remain best effort and V2 controls do not fetch profiles. Eighteen actual-source cases independently regenerate exactly; all18 target PostgreSQL permission-fault/control exchanges and the existing normal profile-source regression pass at root. Package community192, all-targets and module checks pass. Missing-profile row semantics, other dependency failures, deployed cache state and cutover remain separate verification. |
| `private-call-stale-media-coexistence` | unverified | Actual Social/companion PostgreSQL components and the candidate permit a new pending call when retained media presence is initial-expired, interrupted-expired or disconnected. Six lifecycle cases and two media-writer sequences are independently recaptured exactly. Candidate credentials retain older pending/media rows; actual join and explicit end own cleanup by call identity. Explicit READ COMMITTED and ordered normalized-wallet locks preserve one pending across roles under a REPEATABLE READ role default. The explicit schema-version-3 release procedure preserves data and gates older binaries; package voice55, Comms private15, database7 and owned schema-upgrade5 tests pass. Aggregate validation, production migration, live media and cutover remain separate evidence requirements. |
| `community-client-write-failure-phases` | unverified | Client BAN and update preserve the source commit phases on the existing pool: completed membership/unlike/analytics stages survive a later ban/request failure, while community updates precede separate places and atomic bulk acceptance. Nine actual-source PostgreSQL trigger captures independently match exactly; package community186 tests pass. Native federation and atomic join retain their separate contracts. Production crash/retry/concurrency and nonempty cutover remain unverified. Community-scoped native advisory guards coordinate joins, all acceptance paths, BAN and ownership SQL transfer while retaining separate source commit stages. Cancellation/error and queued owner/BAN cases pass local PostgreSQL barriers; this strengthens concurrency coordination beyond source. Acquisition has an absolute one-second budget including pool checkout and a 750ms local server lock timeout; an interrupted connection is closed until temporary transaction completion is confirmed. SQLx 0.9 native acquire was already cancellation-safe. This bounds retention and differs from unlimited source waits; existing separate commit phases remain. The real PostgreSQL COMMIT-response barrier exercises caller cancellation, helper deadline and real SQL-error cleanup: backend disappearance precedes relay release, independent same-key acquisition and a clean maxpool1 replacement succeed, and protected join writes never run. This direct-join proof does not execute every other handler at that wire boundary. |
| `community-voice-raw-cache-aliases` | unverified | One authoritative case-sensitive raw-key relation preserves independent alias scopes, generation CAS and exact expirations; canonical UUID remains media/membership identity. Four independently regenerated source lifecycles and four PostgreSQL-backed regressions cover raw RPC/JSON/SNS identity, restarts, expiry, stale-generation interleavings and bounded polling; actual Comms presence checks active aliases. The composed schema3 release shares canonical table/index DDL and accepts shipped main-v2 without0020 or genuinely prepared v2 with its unchanged real receipt. It atomically transfers/verifies/retires legacy facts when present, creates replacement indexes before stamp3 and never fabricates a retired receipt. Owned-database tests cover both genuine origins, refusal, connection-loss rollback/retry, executor/indexes/bootstrap, all five retired objects and immutable ledgers. Original raw aliases cannot be recovered from older UUID-only facts; production Redis import/drain, room continuity and cutover/rollback are unverified. No architecture or deployment acceptance is inferred. |
| `community-recipient-pagination-and-exclusions` | unverified | SNS recipient pagination orders role,joined_at,member_address, giving tied rows a deterministic final order beyond source. The generic helper excludes every address with ALL; the pinned source ANY predicate differs for2+ distinct exclusions. Current production post/voice strategies each provide one exclusion, so no current public operation with that multi-exclusion difference is asserted. A real PostgreSQL230-member tied-page case verifies complete unique delivery; concurrent membership changes across pages remain unverified. |
